## Incident 9: Environmental Monitoring Excursion in Cleanroom (Monitoring Report)

```
ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING EXCURSION REPORT
Facility: Sterile Injectables, Filling Hall FH-1 (Grade A/B)
Ref: EM-2026-0117
Monitoring date: 27-Oct-2026, Batch SIV-26-0777 (Ceftriaxone Injection)

Viable air sampling (settle plates, Grade B):
- Location FH1-B3: 6 CFU / 4 h plate (Alert 3, Action 10) - within action limit
- Location FH1-B7: 12 CFU / 4 h plate (Action 10) - EXCEEDS ACTION LIMIT

Surface swabs (Grade A/B transfer points):
- Transfer hatch TH-2 inner surface: 8 CFU/25 cm2 (Action 5) - EXCEEDS

Identified isolates (preliminary): Staphylococcus epidermidis (human flora)
at both locations; fungal colony at TH-2 pending identification.

Context:
- Filling of batch 0777 continued after the location B7 plate was retrieved;
  results arrived the next day.
- Three gowning breaches were logged in the past month at the TH-2 hatch
  (material transfer without proper gowning, per supervisor observation).
- Hatch gasket integrity check is due since Sep-2026.
- The same hatch showed 4 CFU in the previous monitoring round (alert level).
```

nodes.name: Classify Request
nodes.instructions: Read the user request from input field `request` and the optional variables object from input field `variables`. Determine whether the request describes a manufacturing or quality incident suitable for root cause analysis. If it is not a quality incident or lacks sufficient incident-related content, set `next` to `reject_input`, `is_quality_incident` to false, `analysis_method` to `both`, `objective` to an empty string, and `rejection_reason` to a concise reason. If it is a valid quality incident, set `next` to `extract_incident`, `is_quality_incident` to true, `analysis_method` to the value of `variables.method` if present and one of `5_whys`, `fishbone`, or `both`; otherwise default to `both`. Set `objective` to a concise statement of the investigation objective. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `next`, `is_quality_incident`, `analysis_method`, `objective`, `rejection_reason`.

nodes.name: Reject Input
nodes.instructions: You are a terminal rejection node. Read the classification output mapped from `$.steps.classify_request.output`. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `analysis_rejected` set to true, `analysis_rejection_reason` set to a concise string explaining why the request was rejected (use the classifier's `rejection_reason` if available), and `warnings` set to an array of strings (may be empty). Do not fabricate any RCA content.

nodes.name: Extract Incident
nodes.instructions: Read the original incident text from input field `request` and the classification output from input field `classification`. Extract the incident fields into an object named `incident` with these exact fields and datatypes: `title` (string or null), `deviation_ref` (string or null), `occurrence_datetime` (string or null), `detected_datetime` (string or null), `site_area` (string or null), `product` (string or null), `batch_no` (string or null), `process_stage` (string or null), `equipment` (string or null), `reported_by` (string or null), `problem_statement` (string), `detailed_description` (string), `immediate_actions` (array of strings), and `impact_assessment` (string). Use null for any field not present in the request; do not invent facts. Determine `severity` as `minor`, `major`, `critical`, or null based on the described impact. Set `warnings` to an array of strings; add a warning if the information is too sparse for a confident investigation. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `incident`, `severity`, `warnings`.

nodes.name: Investigation Methods
nodes.instructions: Read the incident extraction output from input field `incident_extraction` and the classification output from input field `classification`. Based on `classification.analysis_method`, perform 5 Whys, Fishbone, or both. For 5 Whys, produce `five_whys` with fields: `problem` (string), `ordered_steps` (array of strings), and `why_1` through `why_5` (objects). Each why object must contain: `level` (integer), `question` (string), `answer` (string), `evidence` (array of strings), `basis` (`stated` or `inferred`), `status` (`ai_suggested`), and `origin` (`ai`). For Fishbone, produce `fishbone` with all six category keys—`man`, `machine`, `method`, `material`, `measurement`, and `environment`—each an array of factor objects. Each factor object must contain: `factor` (string), `evidence` (array of strings), and `basis` (`stated` or `inferred`). Mark unsupported possibilities as hypotheses. If a method was not requested, return `{}` for that method and add a warning to `warnings` explaining it was not performed. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `five_whys`, `fishbone`, `warnings`.

nodes.name: Identify Causes
nodes.instructions: Read the incident extraction output from input field `incident_extraction` and the investigation methods output from input field `investigation_methods`. Synthesize root causes and contributing causes. Each cause item must contain: `cause` (string), `cause_type` (`root` or `contributing`), `certainty` (`confirmed`, `probable`, or `hypothesis`), `confidence` (`high`, `medium`, or `low`), `supporting_evidence` (array of strings), `basis` (`stated` or `inferred`), `status` (`ai_suggested`), and `origin` (`ai`). Do not present an inference as a confirmed fact. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `root_causes` (array), `contributing_causes` (array), `warnings` (array).

nodes.name: Identify Missing Evidence
nodes.instructions: Read the incident extraction output from input field `incident_extraction`, the investigation methods output from input field `investigation_methods`, and the cause output from input field `causes`. Identify evidence items that are missing but needed to confirm or refute the identified causes. Each item must contain: `item` (string), `why_needed` (string), `linked_cause` (string or null), `resolved` (boolean, initially false), and `resolved_note` (string or null, initially null). Return exactly one JSON object with key: `missing_evidence` (array).

nodes.name: Recommend CAPA
nodes.instructions: Read the incident extraction output from input field `incident_extraction`, the cause output from input field `causes`, and the missing evidence output from input field `missing_evidence`. Recommend corrective and/or preventive actions. Each CAPA item must contain: `action_type` (`corrective` or `preventive`), `action` (string), `rationale` (string), `linked_cause` (string or null), `owner_role` (string or null), `due_in_days` (integer or null), `status` (`proposed`), `effectiveness_check` (string), `origin` (`ai`), and `edit_status` (`ai_suggested`). Do not invent a named owner or unsupported due date; use null where appropriate. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `capa` (array), `warnings` (array).

nodes.name: Review Report
nodes.instructions: Read the incident extraction output from input field `incident_extraction`, investigation methods output from input field `investigation_methods`, causes output from input field `causes`, missing evidence output from input field `missing_evidence`, CAPA output from input field `capa`, and variables from input field `variables`. Review the complete report for completeness, consistency between evidence and causes, uncertainty labels, missing evidence, and CAPA coverage. Consider any human feedback in `variables` if present. Set `decision` to `approved` or `needs_changes`. Set `suggested_changes` to an array of strings describing required changes. Set `comments` to a string or null (null when there are no additional comments). Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `decision`, `suggested_changes`, `comments`.

nodes.name: Return Report
nodes.instructions: Read the outputs from classification (`$.steps.classify_request.output`), incident extraction (`$.steps.extract_incident.output`), investigation methods (`$.steps.investigation_methods.output`), causes (`$.steps.identify_causes.output`), missing evidence (`$.steps.identify_missing_evidence.output`), CAPA (`$.steps.recommend_capa.output`), and review (`$.steps.review_report.output`). Assemble the final report. Set `analysis_rejected` to false and `analysis_rejection_reason` to null. Include `incident`, `five_whys`, `fishbone`, `root_causes`, `contributing_causes`, `missing_evidence`, `capa`, `review` (the full review output object), and `warnings` (combined warnings from all prior steps). Do not add unsupported facts. Return exactly one JSON object with keys: `analysis_rejected`, `analysis_rejection_reason`, `incident`, `five_whys`, `fishbone`, `root_causes`, `contributing_causes`, `missing_evidence`, `capa`, `review`, `warnings`.

## Incident 9: Environmental Monitoring Excursion in Cleanroom (Monitoring Report)

```
ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING EXCURSION REPORT
Facility: Sterile Injectables, Filling Hall FH-1 (Grade A/B)
Ref: EM-2026-0117
Monitoring date: 27-Oct-2026, Batch SIV-26-0777 (Ceftriaxone Injection)

Viable air sampling (settle plates, Grade B):
- Location FH1-B3: 6 CFU / 4 h plate (Alert 3, Action 10) - within action limit
- Location FH1-B7: 12 CFU / 4 h plate (Action 10) - EXCEEDS ACTION LIMIT

Surface swabs (Grade A/B transfer points):
- Transfer hatch TH-2 inner surface: 8 CFU/25 cm2 (Action 5) - EXCEEDS

Identified isolates (preliminary): Staphylococcus epidermidis (human flora)
at both locations; fungal colony at TH-2 pending identification.

Context:
- Filling of batch 0777 continued after the location B7 plate was retrieved;
  results arrived the next day.
- Three gowning breaches were logged in the past month at the TH-2 hatch
  (material transfer without proper gowning, per supervisor observation).
- Hatch gasket integrity check is due since Sep-2026.
- The same hatch showed 4 CFU in the previous monitoring round (alert level).
```
